body.en:
Question B-006-004-004.

Why the correct answer is right: For the same cable and frequency, every additional metre adds some attenuation. Therefore total signal loss increases as the transmission line gets longer.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Signal loss decreases as the length increases": This reverses the physical trend; a longer lossy path cannot have less total attenuation just because it is longer.
- sourceIndex 2: "Signal loss is the least when the length is the same as the signal's wavelength": A wavelength-long line may repeat some impedance conditions, but it still has the loss of its full physical length.
- sourceIndex 3: "Signal loss is the same for any length of transmission line": Equal cable type and frequency do not make a 5 m run lose the same power as a 50 m run.
